correctness.rationale: The fair-bit Hamiltonicity condition is strict positivity of every reversed partial sum. The clique identity counts the 1 bits plus the initial vertex, and edge counting with weight j on creation bit j gives the sum of the reversed partial sums with the stated normalization. The interpolated area differs from that sum divided by L^(3/2) by at most 1/(2 sqrt(L)). With r trailing 1 bits off the complete graph, the graph is the join of K_r and a disconnected remainder (the last vertex of the remainder was added isolated); the Laplacian spectrum of the join gives lambda_2=r, including zero for a disconnected graph. The exceptional complete graph has lambda_2=n, yielding the extra 2^(-L) needed for the exact unconditioned mean 1. Reflection at zero from height a subtracts binom(t,j+a) for an endpoint reached by j up-steps, and summation telescopes to B(t,a). The exact-r prefix is r up-steps then a down-step, leaving height r-1 and time L-r-1; the all-up word has its separate mass. Central-binomial asymptotics give (r-1)2^(-r). For the claimed uniform tail, the at-least-r prefix count is B(L-r,r); for r<=L/2 use the central-binomial bound, and for r>L/2 use B(L-r,r)<=2^(L-r) and sqrt(L)<=2r. This also controls moments, with the complete-graph moment correction exponentially small. Conditional on any fixed exact-r prefix, the surviving continuation is a walk from fixed positive height, with the same finite-horizon meander limit; the prefix vanishes on rescaling. Tightness allows summing over r, proving independence from the entire path, not just its endpoint or area. The latter two are dependent: the meander bridge at endpoint y has the law of a three-dimensional Bessel bridge to y (the positive Brownian kernel and its h-transform have the same bridges), so by convexity of the norm its expected area is at least y/2. This cannot be constant over the unbounded endpoint law.
residual_risks: Finite enumeration does not check process convergence. The finite-horizon meander invariance principle is a classical analytic input, not a machine-checked result. For the fixed-positive-start variant one may also decompose the walk by first attainment of its minimum increment level: its finitely many allowed minimum levels have first-hit mass O((h+1)^(-3/2)), and subsequent nonnegative survival is O((L-h+1)^(-1/2)). Dividing by the order L^(-1/2) survival probability gives tightness of that first-hit time, reducing the limit to the ordinary meander started at zero.

value.rationale: Hamiltonicity is a natural rare-event conditioning that changes an actual graph invariant: the limiting spectral mean is 4 rather than 1, and the entire conditional spectral law is available at finite order, including the complete graph. The joint theorem separates a local spectral statistic from all continuous path functionals while retaining the dependence of the global endpoint and area. Neither the finite spectral comparison nor that joint interpretation is supplied by quoting the separate global and unconditioned spectral laws. The added value is this conditioned exact distribution and local/global separation, not the standard walk tools.
residual_risks: Specific to the fair-bit model and strict Hamiltonicity condition; no claim of finite-order independence or a rate of joint convergence.
